scope: Proposition 2.2 (Free exhaustion limit) of the manuscript “The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID” (preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 231 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 478f5137621e0b3b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be an infinite connected locally finite simple graph. If H1 ⊆ H2 ⊆ · · · are finite connected subgraphs with S n E(Hn) = E(G), the uniform spanning-tree laws on Hn, extended by absent edges outside Hn, converge weakly on {0, 1}E(G). Their limit is independent of the exhaustion, is supported on spanning forests, and is transported by every graph isomorphism. We denote this law by FUSFG.
